claim_boundary: C018 adds four descendants born from exact attacks. H121 and H122 package an explicit high-treewidth local-twin construction and its treewidth transfer; H123 and H124 remain open. No P-versus-NP result is claimed.

hypotheses.title: Exact Toroidal Tseitin Local SAT-UNSAT Twin Lemma Candidate
hypotheses.statement: For every fixed signed-incidence radius R, let m=8R+13 and take two disjoint copies of the m by m toroidal grid. Encode one degree-four Tseitin parity equation at every grid vertex using edge variables. The SAT member places two unit charges in one component and none in the other; the UNSAT member places one unit charge in each component. The formulas have opposite satisfiability, exactly equal translation-normalized rooted signed-incidence neighborhood multisets through radius R, and primal treewidth at least m-1.
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: The explicit-construction half of H119 is achieved with linear treewidth: fixed-radius local views cannot detect whether two charges occupy one component or are split between components, while the identity compiler no longer meets an O(log n) treewidth target.
hypotheses.proof_role: ADVERSARIAL_TARGET: upgrade H118 from treewidth two to a high-treewidth Tseitin family while preserving exact local equality and opposite component parity.
hypotheses.next_gate: Obtain independent review of the universal local-signature counting argument and then prove a factorization theorem for every H106 low-treewidth transduction on this family.
hypotheses.delta_from_parents: H121 replaces H118's two cycles by two toroidal grids, retains the same charge-distribution indistinguishability mechanism, and raises primal treewidth from two to Omega(m).
falsification_conditions: A radius R for which the complete rooted signed-neighborhood multisets differ.
A satisfying assignment for the odd-charge member or failure of the even-charge spanning-tree assignment.
Failure of the primal graph to equal two copies of the line graph of the toroidal grid.
A published treewidth transfer not supporting the claimed m-1 lower bound.
hypotheses.claim_boundary: H121 constructs hard-looking inputs but does not prove that every constant-pass compiler loses the global charge distribution.

hypotheses.title: Toroidal Tseitin Primal Treewidth Transfer Lemma Candidate
hypotheses.statement: For the standard edge-variable CNF encoding of a Tseitin system on a graph G, the primal graph is exactly the line graph L(G): two variables occur together precisely when their graph edges share a vertex. Consequently tw(primal) is at least (tw(G)+1)/2-1. For the m by m toroidal grid, whose treewidth is 2m-1 for m at least five, the H121 primal graph has treewidth at least m-1.
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: H121 rigorously excludes the identity compiler and every output retaining the full input primal graph from the O(log n)-treewidth class targeted by H106.
hypotheses.proof_role: DIRECT_BRIDGE: connect the explicit Tseitin CNF syntax to published toroidal-grid and line-graph treewidth theorems.
hypotheses.next_gate: Receive independent verification that the chosen degree-four CNF creates every and only line-graph adjacency and record the precise disconnected-union treewidth convention.
hypotheses.delta_from_parents: H122 isolates the external graph-theoretic transfer needed to turn H121's toroidal base into a certified linear primal-treewidth lower bound.
falsification_conditions: A pair of Tseitin edge variables sharing a clause without sharing a graph endpoint.
Two incident graph edges absent from every local parity clause.
An incorrect application of the published line-graph or toroidal-grid treewidth bounds.
hypotheses.claim_boundary: The lemma is a treewidth statement only and supplies no transduction lower bound by itself.

hypotheses.title: Toroidal Charge-Quotient Factorization Conjecture
hypotheses.statement: For every fixed-pass radius-bounded H106 transduction applied to the H121 toroidal Tseitin pair, if both outputs have polynomial size and O(log n) primal treewidth, then the output and all local recovery annotations factor through a common bounded quotient determined by the radius-visible torus cover. This quotient cannot retain whether the two unit charges lie in one connected component or in two, so the transduction cannot be equisatisfiable on both members.
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: H106 is refuted on an explicit high-treewidth family, completing the restricted-locality funnel left open by H119.
hypotheses.proof_role: ADVERSARIAL_BRIDGE: turn H121's high-treewidth local twins into a global compiler obstruction through one explicit quotient-factorization theorem.
hypotheses.next_gate: Formalize the exact transduction category and prove that any low-treewidth output admits the claimed common quotient rather than a hidden global component-parity channel.
hypotheses.delta_from_parents: H123 instantiates H119's abstract lift pair with the toroidal Tseitin family and names the sole remaining theorem: low-treewidth factorization through a common local quotient.
falsification_conditions: An H106-legal O(log n)-treewidth output that preserves the split-versus-coincident charge bit.
A recovery annotation carrying global component parity despite bounded ancestry.
Failure of the two H121 inputs to share the required local cover.
hypotheses.claim_boundary: No quotient theorem is currently proved; OPEN records a sharply localized missing bridge, not evidence that the bridge exists.

hypotheses.title: Length-Normalized Sound-Circuit SAT Anti-Checker Conjecture
hypotheses.statement: For every constant k there is a deterministic algorithm polynomial in the actual canonical formula length L that, on input 1^L, outputs a polynomial-size list of pairs (F,a) with every F encoded in exactly L bits and a satisfying F, such that every SAT-sound Boolean circuit on L-bit formula encodings of size at most L^k rejects at least one listed F.
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: If SAT had circuit size L^c, choose k greater than c. The exact SAT circuit is SAT-sound and would have size at most L^k, contradicting H124. Hence SAT is not in P/poly and P != NP.
hypotheses.proof_role: DIRECT_TARGET: repair H116 by measuring generation time, formula length, and circuit size with the same actual input-length parameter.
hypotheses.next_gate: Construct a length-exact positive list with witness diversity beyond H120 and prove incompressibility against every L^k-size SAT-sound circuit without testing soundness.
hypotheses.delta_from_parents: H124 removes H116's circular n-versus-L exponent comparison by fixing formulas at exactly L bits and quantifying circuit size as L^k.
falsification_conditions: For some k, an L^k-size SAT-sound circuit covers every generated list for infinitely many L.
The generator pads formulas in a way that changes the quantified input domain or hides superpolynomial work.
The H120 witness-cover circuit remains within L^k.
hypotheses.claim_boundary: The repaired implication to P != NP is formal, but no anti-checker construction or circuit lower bound is known.
